title: This is a card
subtitle: Every row in the table becomes one of these
body:
## Here's the deal

This is libelli. It turns every row of a spreadsheet into a printed card, and that's the whole trick. The table holds the words, this page holds the design, and you never have to line the two up by hand again.

Go ahead and change *This is a card* in the table. The title changes as you type, because it isn't a copy of the cell — it *is* the cell.

- **Bring your own rows.** Copy cells straight out of Excel, Sheets or Numbers and paste them in. No header row, no clean-up.
- **It stays here.** No account, no upload, no server. Your data never leaves this browser.

Point your phone at the corner and libelli opens there too.

title: Cells can do more than words
subtitle: Markdown, colour, and the art of leaving things out
body:
## Formatting without a toolbar

Any cell can carry **bold**, *italic*, ~~strikethrough~~, `code`, lists and [links](https://heracl.es/libelli). Want a few words in colour? Write `[this]{red}` and you get [this]{red}. Hex, `rgb()` and names like [green]{green} or [purple]{purple} all work, and `red` prints as a printer's red rather than your screen's.

That band down the edge is a column too. Type `orange` into this row's `accent` cell and watch it change.

## Notice what's missing

This row has no link, so **there's no QR code in the corner**. An area set to *Hide When Empty* doesn't leave a hole behind; it just gets out of the way.

title: Nothing on this page is stuck
subtitle: Drag it, restyle it, or start over from your own columns
body:
## Everything moves

Drag any area, or grab a corner to resize it. Make this title absurdly long and the text below moves down, because it's anchored to the title rather than pinned in place. Run out of room and the area's corner turns red, so you find out before the printer does.

## Style is per area

That sticker is a drawing stored in the row itself, turned a few degrees, with a border drawn by hand. Double-click it to draw your own, or select anything and the bar above shows how it's made.

## Keep more than one design

The caret beside **Template** holds every design you save. Start a new one and the button with three shapes reads your columns and lays out a first draft for you.

title: Take it with you
subtitle: On paper, as a picture, or as a booklet
body:
## Print it

Hit **Print** or Ctrl/Cmd+P for a preview of every sheet. Turn on background graphics so the colours make it onto the paper.

## Or fold it into a zine

These four cards make exactly one booklet. They already have left and right pages, which is why the page numbers sit on the outside edge.

1. In the print preview, set **Pages per Sheet** to **2-up** and **Order** to **Zinemaker**.
2. Print double-sided, flipping on the long edge.
3. Fold it in half. Congratulations, you made a zine.

## And the rest

**PNG** saves a card as an image. **Export** saves just the design, small enough to send in a message. **Install** gives libelli its own window, and it works offline.

Want this tour back? Press and hold **Import CSV…**.
